questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank.**

The detective's investigation was __thorough__ and __________ , leaving no stone unturned.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**meticulous**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's take a look at the given words:
 
 
• **Thorough**: complete with regard to every detail; not superficial or partial.

 
 
• **Sentence**: The analysis was very **thorough**.
 
 
 
• **Careless**: not paying attention; not careful
 
 
• **Sentence**: The **careless** driver caused a car accident.
 
 
 
• **Meticulous**: very careful and precise
 
 
• **Sentence**: The **meticulous **scientist made sure to double-check their data.
 
 
 
• **Imprecise**: not accurate or exact
 
 
• **Sentence**: The **imprecise** measurement resulted in incorrect calculations.
 
 
 
• **Inaccurate**: not accurate; not correct
 
 
• **Sentence**: The **inaccurate** report contained many mistakes.
 
 
 
 
 
• From the given meanings and examples, we can conclude that "**careless**," "**imprecise**," and "**inaccurate**" are not synonyms for "**thorough**."
 
• Thus, ***option 2: meticulous*** is the correct synonym.

**The correct sentence is**__: "*The detective's investigation was thorough and **meticulous**, leaving no stone unturned.*"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• Thorough: हर विवरण के संबंध में पूरा; सूक्ष्म या आंशिक नहीं।
 
• Careless: ध्यान न देना; सावधान नहीं
 
• Meticulous: बहुत सावधान और सुनिश्चित
 
• Imprecise: सुनिश्चित या सटीक नहीं
 
• Inaccurate: सही नहीं; गलत
 
• दिए गए अर्थ और उदाहरणों से हम निश्चित हो सकते हैं कि "careless," "imprecise," और "inaccurate" "thorough" के समानार्थी शब्द नहीं हैं।
 
• इसलिए, *meticulous *सही समानार्थी शब्द है।.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

The heavy medications and strong drugs at the sanatorium will surely turn a patient __completely lifeless and unresponsive.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. "cadaverous".

• **Example: ** After weeks of illness, he had a cadaverous appearance.
 
 
 
• **"Cadaverous"** captures the essence of being lifeless and unresponsive due to the severe effects of medications or illness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Cadaverous**.

• **Example: **The zonic climate varies significantly across the region.

• **Example:** He looked wasted after days without food.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• The given word **'Obvious'** means something which is easily perceived or understood; clear, self-evident, or apparent. ('स्पष्ट' or 'प्रत्यक्ष').

 
 
• **Example:** The benefits of the decision were obvious to everyone.
 
 
 
• **'Ambiguous' **means something which is open to more than one interpretation. ('अस्पष्ट' or 'संदिग्ध').
 
 
• **Example:** The language in the contract was ambiguous and led to different interpretations.

• **'Inherent' **refers to something that is a basic or essential part of something; it's unremovable. ('सहज' or 'निहित').
 
• **'Apparent'** refers to things that are clearly visible or understood; obvious. ('प्रत्यक्ष' or 'स्पष्ट').

questions.question:
Complete the sentence with the most appropriate set of ANTONYMS of the highlighted word.

'Grisly'

The other day Jimmy behaved ______ with Jammy and that was quite ______ for me.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Grisly"** means something that is causing horror or disgust. (भयानक)
 
 
• **Example: **The grisly scene of the accident left everyone in shock.
 
 
 
• **"Pleasantly"** refers to something that is enjoyable, pleasing, or agreeable. (सुखद)
 
 
• **Example: **She was pleasantly surprised by the unexpected gift.
 
 
 
• **"Comforting"** means providing comfort or solace. (सांत्वना देने वाला)
 
 
• **Example: **His comforting words helped ease her anxiety.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the antonyms of **'Grisly'** are **'Pleasantly'** and **'Comforting'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Rudely, attractive**
 
 
• **Rudely** (असभ्यतापूर्वक): In an impolite or disrespectful manner.
 
 
• **Example:** He rudely interrupted the speaker in the middle of the presentation.
 
 
 
• **Attractive** (आकर्षक): Pleasing or appealing to the senses.
 
 
• **Example:** The garden was filled with attractive flowers and plants.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Disgusting, atrocious**
 
 
• **Disgusting** (घिनौना): Arousing revulsion or strong indignation.
 
 
• **Example:** The food was disgusting and had a foul odor.
 
 
 
• **Atrocious** (क्रूर): Horrifyingly wicked or of a very poor quality.
 
 
• **Example:** The atrocious crime shocked the entire community.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Ghastly, shameless**
 
 
• **Ghastly** (भयानक): Causing great horror or fear.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the correct collocation.**

Of course, we agree with that measure, it is _________ sensible.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** perfectly.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct collocation to be used here is **perfectly**.
 
• **Collocation **is two or more words that often go together.
 
• The collocation to be used here is: **adverb + adjective.**
 
• Example: 
 
 
• Are you **fully aware** of the consequences of leaving the company now? 
 
 
 
• The phrase **"perfectly sensible" **means **completely reasonable, logical, or rational.**
 
 
• Example sentence: The decision to extend the deadline for the project was **perfectly sensible** given the unforeseen circumstances.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

**Correct Sentence:**__* Of course, we agree with that measure, it is **__perfectly__** sensible.***​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• Other **types of collocations **are:

 
• adjective + noun (excruciating pain)
 
• noun + noun (round of applause)
 
• noun + verb (bomb went off)
 
• verb + noun (commit suicide)
 
• verb + expression with preposition (burst into tears)
 
• verb + adverb (wave frantically)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Both the parties will be _______ benefitted by this deal in the long run.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "mutually".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Let's analyse each given option:**

 
 
• **"Mutually"** refers to a situation where two or more parties benefit from the same action or arrangement. Therefore, this **would fit **in the sentence as it implies that **both parties benefit from the deal, **which aligns with the context.
 
• **"Agreeably" **refers to something **that's pleasant or pleases people. **While a business deal might be agreeable, it **doesn't make sense **in this specific context as the **sentence is about how both parties will benefit, **and not about the pleasant nature of the deal.
 
• **"Respectively" **is used to indicate something that follows a certain order previously established in the sentence. It **doesn't fit in this context **as there's **no such order established regarding the parties' benefiting from the deal.**
 
• **"Unilaterally" **means that something is done by one person or party alone without the agreement or participation of others. This wouldn't work as the sentence implies the deal will benefit both parties involved.
 
 
 
• Hence, in the context of the sentence **"Both the parties will be _______ benefited by this deal in the long run", **the word fits best, as it conveys that** both parties are set to gain benefits from the deal.**
 
• The **correctly filled sentence **would read: ***"Both the parties will be mutually__ benefitted by this deal in the long run."***

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**
